reason: The liver-cell picture shows glucose entering from blood and being joined into a stored carbohydrate.
expectation: The liver cells will store some of the meal's glucose.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the digestive organs is the other goal, but I can start with the glucose store.

effect: The liver cells stored some glucose as linked carbohydrate, completing the storage goal.
reaction: The picture makes the store easier to understand.
reason: The remaining goal is to connect the digestive organs to the body, and these two pieces match it.
expectation: The digestive tract will connect to the body and its circulation.

effect: The digestive tract is now connected to the body's circulation, completing the chapter; the colon's inner wall remains unfinished.
reaction: The connection was straightforward, though the unfinished wall made me curious.

mostWorthwhile.text: Storing glucose in liver cells was most worthwhile: the picture showed individual glucose units joining into a store that can be broken down later.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the digestive tract was useful but predictable; the goal and available pieces made the pairing obvious.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected the completed body model to still show an unfinished inner colon wall.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: both matched a stated goal and the pictures explained their purpose.

continue.text: I would continue, mainly to see how the unfinished colon wall fits into the digestive system, although this short chapter had few meaningful choices.
